rules.title: Cash is still king
rules.summary: Many taxis, louages, and small cafés prefer or require cash (TND). Keep small notes.
rules.details: ATMs are common in Houmt Souk and Midoun. Airport ATMs may have queues and fees.

rules.title: Agree taxi fare before leaving
rules.summary: Especially from the airport and at night — confirm price before boarding.
rules.details: Official ranks are safer than random offers. Louage (shared taxi) uses fixed-ish per-seat prices on known routes.

rules.title: Modest dress in towns and religious sites
rules.summary: Beachwear is for beaches/hotels. Cover shoulders/knees in medina and at El Ghriba.

rules.title: Night travel — stick to lit tourist corridors
rules.summary: Prefer hotel taxis at night; avoid empty industrial stretches if alone.
rules.details: Ask your hotel for trusted drivers. Share location with someone if traveling late.

rules.title: Pharmacie de garde (night pharmacy)
rules.summary: Night pharmacy rota rotates — ask hotel reception or police for tonight’s location.

rules.title: Airport SIM desks
rules.summary: Buy a local SIM after landing if you need data for maps and taxis.
rules.details: Bring passport for registration. Compare Tunisie Telecom / Ooredoo / Orange offers.

rules.title: Unsolicited “helpers” at airport
rules.summary: Politely decline random luggage helpers and unofficial taxi offers; use the marked rank.

rules.title: Ask before photographing people
rules.summary: Especially in markets and villages — a smile and ask goes far.

rules.title: Emergency numbers (Tunisia)
rules.details: Save these offline. Hotel reception can also call a trusted clinic.

rules.title: Alcohol availability varies
rules.summary: Hotel bars and some restaurants serve alcohol; many local cafés do not.
